html:
The car made by the Ford Motor Company from 1908 to 1927, the first car that ordinary people could afford. About 15 million were built, a record that stood for decades.

Henry Ford designed it to be simple, tough and easy to repair, with high ground clearance for the muddy country roads of the time. Farmers used it to haul goods and even to run farm machines.

The key was how it was made. In 1913 Ford's Highland Park plant near Detroit began using a moving assembly line, which brought the work to the worker. The time to build a car fell from about twelve hours to about an hour and a half. The price fell year after year, from 850 dollars at launch to under 300 in the 1920s. For years it came only in black, because black paint dried fastest.

Ford built plants abroad, including in Britain and Canada, and the method spread to every industry as Fordism. The car remade American life, bringing roads, suburbs, petrol stations and later the Interstate Highway System.
